rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **kinetic molecular model** states that a gas is a vast number of identical molecules in rapid random motion, and that its **pressure is the collective bombardment of the container walls** while its **temperature measures the average molecular kinetic energy**.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Low Density Required: Model assumes molecular volume ≪ container volume. Valid when gas is dilute (low P, high T). Breaks down near condensation point.  ·  Elastic Collisions Only: Energy conservation in collisions is essential. Inelastic collisions would cause temperature decay — not observed in equilibrium gases.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The pressure of a gas arises from the bombardment of the container walls by its molecules."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Tyre wall*** — steady pressure from ~10²³ molecular collisions per second.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **'Ideal' means the assumptions hold:** point molecules, elastic collisions, no forces — real gases approximate this at low P, high T.  ·  **Pressure is statistical:** no single molecule sustains it; 10²³ collisions per second average into a steady push.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Pressure from a Billion Collisions A tyre wall feels steady pressure, yet it is being bombarded by ~10²³ molecules per second. The kinetic molecular model builds gas behaviour from pure mechanics: elastic collisions of point molecules with the walls. Its five assumptions and one postulate are a 5-mark NEB favourite.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 The kinetic theory — statement and assumptions (5m) **Statement:** a gas consists of a very large number of molecules in rapid, random motion; the pressure exerted by the gas arises from the continuous bombardment of the container walls by these molecules, and temperature measures the average kinetic energy of molecular motion. **Assumptions:** 1.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Write the statement, then number the assumptions 1–6."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short (2m): Which two assumptions fail for a real gas at high pressure?** — Point-molecule volume (molecules occupy finite volume) and negligible intermolecular forces (attractions become significant) — the van der Waals corrections.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The identical 5m question appeared in two consecutive years — near-certain to repeat.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The 5m repeat question (2023, 2024)** — memorise the assumption list verbatim.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Statement: pressure = wall bombardment; temperature ∝ average KE.  ·  Six assumptions: identical point molecules; random motion; elastic collisions; negligible intermolecular forces; Newton's laws; huge N.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The kinetic theory is one of physics' great reductions: Boyle's and Charles's laws fall out of pure mechanics.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: According to kinetic theory, gas pressure is caused by: → B  ·  Average translational KE per molecule depends on: → C

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Large Number of Molecules: Statistical averaging requires N ≫ 1. Fluctuations become significant for very small systems (nanoscale).  ·  Thermal Equilibrium Assumed: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution applies only at equilibrium. Non-equilibrium flows require Boltzmann transport equation.  ·  Verified PYQs: statement + assumptions (2023, 2024 — 5m each).
